events.label: Marvell Technology Q2 FY27 earnings (after close) — $12.2B Google custom chip deal; sector-breadth read-through
events.note: Added Aug 27 morning: FY27 guided $11.5B (+40% YoY), FY28 ~$16.5B. Google $12.2B custom silicon commitment is the print's central variable. Test: if MRVL confirms custom-silicon demand is accelerating alongside Blackwell infrastructure demand, AI chip spend is sector-wide; if MRVL misses, NVDA's dual-bar beat reads as Blackwell-specific rather than broad AI chip adoption. Polymarket: 88% probability of a beat entering the session.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote Aug 28; NVDA beat as backdrop
events.note: Updated Aug 26 night: NVDA dual-bar beat confirmed (GM 75%, Q3 guide $108B vs. $104.2B expected), providing Warsh the most constructive AI/macro backdrop of any Fed speech since late 2025. Core PCE July 3.3% YoY (in-line); headline 3.7% (slight upside). 10Y fell 10bps to 4.64%; 30Y ~5.15%, 15bps from 5.30% trigger. September hike odds ~33%. Keynote Aug 28 at 10 a.m. ET — first as Fed Chair. Central question: does he frame Canada tariff cost-push (Sept 8 retaliatory tariffs) + headline PCE 3.7% as non-transitory inflation vectors (hawkish), or cite Consumer Confidence Expectations at 68.2 as sufficient justification for a hold? A neutral keynote pushes 30Y toward 5.05-5.10%; a hawkish framing pushes 30Y back above 5.20% into a post-NVDA chip reset. Bessent 'major financial institution' sanction still pending — if announced Thursday before Warsh speaks, an oil spike enters the keynote backdrop.

events.label: Bessent 'major financial institution' sanction — still pending as of Aug 26 close; Iranian crude-financing target
events.note: Updated Aug 26 night: Still pending through Wednesday close. Treasury Secretary Bessent previewed a sanction against a 'major financial institution' conducting business with Iran by week-end. Most plausible target: a non-US bank facilitating Iranian crude purchases — a Chinese institution is the geopolitically significant scenario. Current Brent ~$86.50 (-$7.50 from $94 trigger); a routine entity sanction is absorbed easily at this buffer. A Chinese-bank sanction arriving Thursday before Warsh speaks would push Brent toward $89-91 and combine with the Warsh keynote as simultaneous policy signals. Secondary BTC effect if Chinese-institution targeted.

events.label: AVGO Q3 FY2026 earnings (est.) — through $380 structural support; VMware + AI concentration dual overhang
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: AVGO fell 5% to ~$362 on August 19, breaking through $380 structural support. VMware CVE-2026-59310 active exploitation (361 IPs, 47 countries per Aug 14 disclosure) + 72% AI revenue concentration (~72% of next-quarter sequential growth) create dual overhang. At ~65x trailing P/E, any miss or margin compression compounds. Q3 FY2026 results (est. September 4–5) are the first public accounting of both: VMware remediation costs in financial guidance, enterprise customer commentary on the incident, and AI revenue breadth. $380 is now resistance; $340–350 is the next structured support zone. Monday's chip-sector selloff (Intel -5%, AMD -4%) increases sector contagion risk. Flip: recovery above $380 on volume, or formal VMware incident-containment statement before earnings.

events.label: Canada retaliatory tariffs effective — dairy, appliances, ag equipment, pulp, paper, electronics
events.note: Updated Aug 24 night: Carney confirmed Sept 8 date on track. Aug 24 statement: 'We are at war with the United States'; accused Trump administration of seeking to destroy Canada's core industries (steel, aluminum, autos). Dollar-for-dollar retaliation against US 50% tariffs on $28B of Canadian goods (effective Aug 24). Arrives 8 days before September 16 FOMC. Manufacturing supply-chain stress at 13-month high as of Aug 22 PMI. If Warsh at Jackson Hole (Aug 28) cites Canada-US tariff cascade as an inflation risk, September hike odds above 31% would increase.

events.label: Bessent Treasury long-dated buyback ops begin — $4B+ per op, 10-20yr and 20-30yr bonds
events.note: Added Aug 19 night: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced August 19 the department will double the size of long-dated bond buyback operations, raising the maximum per-operation from $2B to at least $4B for bonds maturing in the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year ranges. Effective September 9, runs through November 4 (end of current refunding quarter). Immediate market impact: 30Y fell 9bps to 5.196% on the announcement. The program provides structural demand support for the long end through the NVDA print (Aug 26), Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29), and into October. If underlying supply dynamics ($432B July deficit, $1.7T corporate issuance) overwhelm the $4B+ buyback, the 30Y could reassert above 5.25% before the program begins.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
